result.title: Knowledge distillation across teacher architectures for compact diabetic retinopathy grading
result.comment: 17 pages, 3 figures, 18 tables. Submitted to PLOS ONE
result.summary: Diabetic retinopathy grading from retinal fundus photographs is important but difficult to deploy on resource-constrained hardware. We conducted a controlled study of offline response-based knowledge distillation for five-class diabetic retinopathy grading on APTOS 2019, comparing ResNet-50, MobileNetV3-Large, and Swin Transformer-Tiny (Swin-T) teachers distilled into a MobileNetV3-Small student. A 3 x 4 x 2 grid of teacher, temperature, and hard-label weight was screened at one seed, while six configurations and the no-distillation baseline were evaluated across three seeds. The highest observed single-seed quadratic weighted kappa was 0.9093 (macro-F1 0.6851) for Swin-T at temperature 4 and hard-label weight 0.7; the corresponding three-seed mean was 0.9024, compared with 0.8804 for the baseline. The student used 1.52 M parameters and 5.94 MB, representing an 18.07x parameter reduction relative to Swin-T. Temperature and hard-label weight effects were teacher- and configuration-dependent, while small performance differences were sensitive to random seed. Knowledge distillation produced a compact student with competitive performance under the evaluated protocol, but independent external validation remains necessary.

AI.brief_summary: 在 APTOS 2019 视网膜眼底图像五级分级任务上，比较三种教师架构的离线 response-based 知识蒸馏，蒸馏得到 1.52 M 参数的 MobileNetV3-Small 学生模型并做多种子评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 属于医学图像分类的模型压缩与部署研究，仅输出单一类别预测，不涉及推理期 latent 状态、视觉证据筛选或动态计算，蒸馏线索也无具体的 LVR 借鉴点。
